subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on BMW engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the S68 across all 2 model applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The S68 is a new-generation V8 fitted to BMW M's flagship performance models — the XM and the G90 M5.

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Gaskets, seals, and bearings as standard on every rebuild, with timing chain components inspected and replaced as required. 48V mild-hybrid system components and hot-vee ancillaries are accounted for as part of the rebuild.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: The S68 is too new for a real-world pattern to have emerged. The hot-vee turbo layout presents a similar packaging challenge to the S63 it replaces, but we don't treat this as a specific failure mode — it's a design characteristic we account for in the rebuild process. Diagnosis is required to establish whether an engine needs repair, rebuild or replacement.

notice.rest: engine-specific case studies with real job details are not yet included on this page - they'll be added once a documented set of completed S68 rebuilds is available to draw from, rather than filled with placeholder examples now.
